newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ERIKSSON AND GALEONE UNDER THREAT FOLLOWING CUP EXITS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ERIKSSON AND GALEONE UNDER THREAT FOLLOWING CUP EXITS.

text.p: Coaches Sven-Goran Eriksson of Sampdoria and Giovanni Galeone of Perugia were both treading on uneasy ground on Thursday after their teams were dumped out of the Italian Cup by lower division opposition.
For Sampdoria, the defeat was particularly embarrasing as they were beaten 2-0 by their second division city rivals Genoa who share their ground. Perugia were knocked out by third division Norecina.
Sampdoria president Enrico Mantovani said after the loss: "My first problem now is to find a way of refunding those Sampdoria fans who bought tickets for tonight's game.

"Tonight we played very badly, like a side from I don't know what division. Everything is now up for discussion and when I say everything, I mean the coach, his assistant, the squad and the team directors".

A disappointed Eriksson, said: "For an hour, they played like a Division One side while we played like a Division Four team. If we continue to play like that, then we're already well on the way to relegation".
Another club owner to lick his wounds was Perugia boss Luciano Gaucci following his side's elimination.
Perugia have already lost to Internazionale, Juventus and AC Milan this season, putting Galeone under intense pressure.

"From now on the team and the coach had better answer with actions. As far as Galeone is concerned, he can pick the side he wants just as long as he remains coach of Perugia. But let one thing be clear. His position has been greatly weakened. I want to win".
